name: Kaziranga National Park
shortDescription: UNESCO World Heritage Site & Global Stronghold of the Great Indian One-Horned Rhino
fullDescription: Spanning 858 sq km across the alluvial floodplains of the Brahmaputra, Kaziranga was declared a UNESCO World Heritage Site in 1985. It shelters over 2,600 Great Indian One-Horned Rhinoceroses—representing over two-thirds of the global population. Kaziranga also boasts one of the highest densities of Royal Bengal Tigers in the world, alongside wild Asiatic water buffaloes, Asian elephants, and the critically endangered Eastern swamp deer (Barasingha).
imageAttribution: Photo: Diganta Talukdar (CC BY-SA 4.0 via Wikimedia Commons)
bestSeason: November to April (Park open for safaris; closed during monsoon)
accessNotes: Guwahati Airport (217 km) / Jorhat Airport (97 km) / Furkating Junction (75 km)
entryFee: Assam Forest Dept official online safari portal (kazirangasafari.in) & Range Counters

shortDescription_hi: यूनेस्को विश्व धरोहर स्थल और एक सींग वाले गैंडे का वैश्विक गढ़
description_hi: ब्रह्मपुत्र के मैदानी इलाकों में 858 वर्ग किमी में फैला काजीरंगा 1985 में यूनेस्को विश्व धरोहर स्थल घोषित किया गया। यहाँ दुनिया के दो-तिहाई से अधिक एक सींग वाले गैंडे सुरक्षित हैं।

name: Charaideo Moidams (Ahom Royal Pyramids)
shortDescription: UNESCO World Heritage Site (2024) — Sacred Vaulted Burial Mounds of the Ahom Kings
fullDescription: Inscribed on the UNESCO World Heritage List in July 2024 as India's 43rd World Heritage property, Charaideo was the first capital established by Chao Lung Siu-Ka-Pha in 1253 CE. The site preserves over 90 vaulted earthen tumuli (Moidams)—hollow vaulted brick-and-stone chambers covered under hemispherical earthen mounds resembling Egyptian pyramids—enshrining the mortal remains of the revered Swargadeos (Ahom Kings) and queens together with their royal regalia.
imageAttribution: Photo: Jim Ankan Deka (CC BY-SA 3.0 via Wikimedia Commons)
bestSeason: October to April (Pleasant dry winter season)
accessNotes: Jorhat Airport (85 km) / Dibrugarh Airport (110 km) / Simaluguri Junction (28 km)
entryFee: Archaeological Survey of India (ASI) ticketed entry at site counter and online

tagline_hi: अहोम राजवंश का पवित्र शाही पिरामिड एवं 2024 यूनेस्को विश्व धरोहर स्थल
shortDescription_hi: अहोम राजवंश का पवित्र शाही पिरामिड एवं 2024 यूनेस्को विश्व धरोहर स्थल
description_hi: चराइदेव असम का पिरामिड कहलाता है। 1253 में चाओलुंग सुकाफा द्वारा स्थापित अहोम साम्राज्य की पहली राजधानी, जहाँ 90 से अधिक शाही समाधियाँ (मैदाम) स्थित हैं।
fullDescription_hi: चराइदेव मैदाम असम के पिरामिड कहे जाते हैं। 1253 में प्रथम अहोम सम्राट चाओलुंग सुकाफा ने चराइदेव में अहोम साम्राज्य की पहली राजधानी बसाई थी। यहाँ अहोम राजाओं और रानियों के 90 से अधिक टीलेनुमा शाही समाधि स्थल मौजूद हैं, जिन्हें 2024 में यूनेस्को विश्व धरोहर का दर्जा दिया गया।

name: Maa Kamakhya Devalaya & Nilachal Hill
shortDescription: Foremost Shakti Peetha of India & Center of Tantric Spiritual Worship
fullDescription: Perched atop sacred Nilachal Hill overlooking the Brahmaputra, Kamakhya is the highest center of Shakti worship in South Asia. In the inner subterranean sanctum (Garbagriha), there is no idol; instead, the goddess is worshipped as a natural yoni-shaped stone fissure fed by an underground perennial spring. Rebuilt by King Nara Narayana of the Koch dynasty in 1565 CE, the temple exhibits the iconic hybrid Nilachal architecture with a multi-sided cruciform base and bee-hive dome spire.

shortDescription_hi: नीलाचल पर्वत पर स्थित 51 शक्तिपीठों में प्रमुख तांत्रिक तीर्थ
description_hi: गुवाहाटी के नीलाचल पर्वत पर स्थित माँ कामाख्या मंदिर 51 शक्तिपीठों में सर्वोच्च स्थान रखता है। यहाँ वार्षिक अम्बुबाची मेला दुनिया भर के भक्तों को आकर्षित करता है।
fullDescription_hi: गुवाहाटी की नीलाचल पहाड़ी पर स्थित माँ कामाख्या धाम भारत के 51 शक्तिपीठों में सबसे पूजनीय है। यहाँ माँ भगवती के महामुद्रा की पूजा की जाती है। प्रतिवर्ष आषाढ़ मास में आयोजित होने वाला अम्बुबाची मेला पूर्वी भारत का सबसे बड़ा धार्मिक समागम है। 1565 में कोच राजा नरनारायण और चिलाराय द्वारा मंदिर का वर्तमान स्वरूप पुनर्निर्मित हुआ था।

name: Rang Ghar (Ahom Royal Amphitheatre)
shortDescription: Asia's Oldest Surviving Sports Pavilion & Architectural Emblem of Assam
fullDescription: Constructed in 1744 CE by the Ahom king Swargadeo Pramatta Singha, Rang Ghar ('House of Entertainment') is considered Asia's oldest surviving amphitheater. The two-storied oval building served as the royal sports pavilion from which Ahom royalty and dignitaries watched traditional sports, wrestling, and buffalo fights during the Rongali Bihu festival. Its distinctive roof is shaped like an inverted Ahom royal longboat adorned with a stone crocodile carving at each end.

shortDescription_hi: अहोम स्वर्गदेवों का 18वीं सदी का शाही खेल रंगमंच एवं एशिया का पहला पैवेलियन
description_hi: शिवसागर में स्थित रंग घर एशिया का पहला ज्ञात खेल रंगमंच है। इसे 1744-1751 के बीच अहोम राजा प्रमत्त सिंह द्वारा भैंसों की लड़ाई और बिहू उत्सव देखने के लिए बनवाया गया था।
fullDescription_hi: शिवसागर में स्थित रंग घर एशिया का पहला ज्ञात शाही खेल पैवेलियन है। 1744-1751 में अहोम राजा प्रमत्त सिंह ने इसका निर्माण कराया था। रूपही पठार में होने वाले पारंपरिक बिहू नृत्य, भैंसों की लड़ाई और कुश्ती का अहोम सम्राट इसी पैवेलियन से अवलोकन करते थे। इसकी छत उलटी हुई शाही नौका के आकार में निर्मित है।

name: Talatal Ghar & Kareng Ghar Royal Palaces
name_hi: Talatal Ghar & Kareng Ghar Royal Palaces
shortDescription: Secret Multi-Level Underground Royal Palace & Military Bastion of the Ahoms
fullDescription: Built by Swargadeo Rudra Singha in 1698 CE and expanded by his successors, Talatal Ghar at Rangpur was the grandest architectural achievement of the Ahom dynasty. The complex consists of seven stories: three underground levels (used as secret escape passages, royal stables, and arsenals) and four upper floors. Nearby Gargaon houses Kareng Ghar, the magnificent multi-tiered wood and brick palace of the Ahom sovereigns.

description_hi: तलातल घर अहोम साम्राज्य का सात मंजिला सैन्य दुर्ग है, जिसके तीन तल पूरी तरह ज़मीन के नीचे गुप्त सुरंगों से जुड़े हुए थे। इसका निर्माण राजा राजेश्वर सिंह ने कराया था।
fullDescription_hi: रंगपुर में स्थित तलातल घर अहोम साम्राज्य का सबसे भव्य सात मंजिला रक्षा दुर्ग है। 1751-1769 के दौरान राजा राजेश्वर सिंह द्वारा निर्मित इस महल के निचले तीन तल पूरी तरह भूमिगत थे, जिनमें गुप्त सुरंगें थीं। यह अहोमों की सैन्य रणनीति और उन्नत निर्माण तकनीक का अद्भुत उदाहरण है।

name: Sivasagar Sivadol & Borpukhuri Lake
shortDescription: Tallest Historical Shiva Temple Tower in India (104 ft) Beside an Imperial Lake
fullDescription: Commissioned in 1734 CE by Queen Bar Raja Ambika, consort of King Shiva Singha, Sivasagar Sivadol stands at an imposing 104 feet (32 meters), making it the tallest historical Shiva temple spire in the Indian subcontinent. It is crowned with an 8-foot pure gold mastaka (Kalasha). The temple stands on the banks of Borpukhuri (Sivasagar tank), an enormous 257-acre artificial lake whose water level naturally stays above the town's ground level.

bestSeason: October to April (Special: Maha Shivaratri in Feb/March draws 300,000 pilgrims)
accessNotes: Sivasagar Town Railway Station (2 km) / Jorhat Airport (55 km)
entryFee: Open entry daily; temple darshan morning and evening

name: Majuli River Island & Sattras
shortDescription: World's Largest Inhabited River Island & Cradle of Neo-Vaishnavite Culture
fullDescription: Formed by the shifting confluence of the Brahmaputra and Subansiri rivers, Majuli is the largest inhabited river island in the world. Established by the 15th-century polymath and social reformer Srimanta Sankardev, Majuli has been the heart of Assam's Neo-Vaishnavite culture for 500 years. It houses living monastic institutions (Sattras), where celibate monks practice ancient Sattriya dance (one of India's 8 classical dances), Ankiya Nat drama, and craft paper-and-bamboo masks.

name: Manas National Park & Biosphere Reserve
shortDescription: UNESCO World Heritage Natural Site, Project Tiger & Golden Langur Biosphere
fullDescription: Located in the foothills of the Eastern Himalayas and contiguous with Royal Manas National Park in Bhutan, Manas covers 950 sq km of pristine alluvial grasslands, semi-evergreen forests, and crystal-clear mountain rivers. It holds five conservation designations: UNESCO World Heritage Site, Project Tiger Reserve, Elephant Reserve, Biosphere Reserve, and Important Bird Area. Famous for rare and endangered endemic species found nowhere else on earth.

name_as: যোৰহাট আৰু ডিব্ৰুগড়ৰ ঐতিহ্যমণ্ডিত চাহ বাগিচা
shortDescription: World's Tea Capital, Heritage Planter Bungalows & Historic 1876 Golf Greens
fullDescription: Assam is the single largest tea-growing region on earth, producing world-renowned malty, rich black teas. Jorhat is known as the 'Tea Capital of the World', where Robert Bruce first discovered native Camellia sinensis var. assamica in 1823. Visitors stay in luxurious 19th-century colonial planter bungalows with expansive verandahs, explore Tocklai Tea Research Institute (the oldest in the world, founded in 1911), and play on historic golf courses.

bestSeason: October to April (Tea harvesting & plucking: April to October)
accessNotes: Jorhat Airport (Rowriah) / Dibrugarh Airport (Mohanbari)
entryFee: Direct booking with Heritage Tea Bungalow properties & Assam Tourism

name_as: নামেৰি ৰাষ্ট্ৰীয় উদ্যান আৰু জিয়া ভৰলী
name_hi: Nameri National Park & Jia Bhoroli River
shortDescription: Angler's Paradise, River Rafting & Stronghold of the White-Winged Wood Duck
fullDescription: Bordering Arunachal Pradesh along the crystal-clear Jia Bhoroli river, Nameri National Park covers 200 sq km of deciduous and semi-evergreen forests. It is one of the few national parks in India that permits walking safaris accompanied by armed forest rangers. Nameri is world-renowned among international ornithologists for over 300 species of birds, including the endangered White-Winged Wood Duck (Deo Hanh, Assam's State Bird) and four hornbill species.
imageAttribution: Photo: Rituraj Dewan (CC BY-SA 4.0 via Wikimedia Commons)
accessNotes: Tezpur Airport (35 km) / Guwahati Airport (195 km)
openingHours: 06:00 - 16:00 daily during season (Forest walking trails by appointment)
entryFee: Assam Forest Dept range office at Potasali entry point

name: Haflong Hill Station & Haflong Lake
shortDescription: Assam's Only Hill Station, Misty Barail Peaks & Emerald Blue Lake
fullDescription: Sitting at an altitude of 680 meters (2,230 ft) in the lush Barail mountain ranges, Haflong is the sole hill station in Assam. With its cool year-round climate, Haflong Lake at the town center with its suspension hanging bridge, pineapple and orange orchards, and rich Dimasa, Zeme Naga, and Hmar tribal traditions, it is celebrated as the 'Scotland of Assam'. Nearby Jatinga valley is famous for its misty vistas and seasonal bird phenomenon.

accessNotes: New Haflong Railway Station (Direct Vistadome train from Guwahati)

name: Umananda Peacock Island & Temple
shortDescription: Smallest Inhabited River Island in the World & Ancient Shiva Shrine
fullDescription: Rising dramatically from the center of the mighty Brahmaputra river right opposite Guwahati's city center, Umananda was christened 'Peacock Island' by British administrators for its plumage-like shape. Built in 1694 CE by Swargadeo Gadadhar Singha, the temple is dedicated to Lord Shiva. The island is recognized by Guinness World Records as the smallest inhabited river island on earth, and is home to a protected group of endangered Golden Langurs.

accessNotes: Guwahati Inland Waterways Ghat (Sukreswar Ghat / Uzanbazar)
entryFee: Nominal ferry ticket at government inland waterways counter

name: Hajo Panchatirtha & Poa Mecca
shortDescription: Sacred Historic Confluence of Hinduism, Buddhism, and Islam
fullDescription: Hajo is an extraordinary historic testament to interfaith harmony in Northeast India. The 16th-century Hayagriva Madhava Temple atop Monikut Hill is revered simultaneously by Hindus as an avatar of Vishnu and by Tibetan and Bhutanese Buddhists (who believe Mahamuni Buddha attained Parinirvana here). Atop adjacent Garurachal Hill rests Poa Mecca, an esteemed 17th-century Sufi pilgrimage shrine built by Mir Lutfullah Shirazi in 1657 CE.
imageAttribution: Photo: Dhruba Jyoti Baruah (CC BY-SA 4.0 via Wikimedia Commons)
accessNotes: Guwahati (30 km by road via Saraighat Bridge)
entryFee: Open entry to all pilgrimages and visitors

name: Pobitora Wildlife Sanctuary
shortDescription: Highest Density of One-Horned Rhinos in the World (Guaranteed Sightings)
fullDescription: Situated just 48 km east of Guwahati, Pobitora Wildlife Sanctuary holds the world's highest density of Great Indian One-Horned Rhinos—over 100 rhinos thriving in just 38.8 sq km of grasslands and alluvial wetlands. Due to the compact size and abundant water bodies, wildlife sightings here are virtually guaranteed. The adjoining Haduk Beel wetland hosts thousands of winter migratory waterfowl.
imageAttribution: Photo: Diganta Talukdar (CC BY-SA 4.0 via Wikimedia Commons)
accessNotes: Guwahati City (48 km by road via Chandrapur route)

name: Tai Phake Buddhist Village & Monastery
shortDescription: Living Tai Buddhist Cultural Heritage & Traditional Stilt Village
fullDescription: Established in 1850 along the meandering banks of the Burhi Dihing river, Namphake is an authentic cultural oasis inhabited by the Tai Phake community, who migrated from Myanmar in the late 18th century. The villagers speak an archaic Tai language, preserve ancient palm-leaf scriptures, and practice Theravada Buddhism. The village features traditional timber and bamboo chang-ghar (stilt homes) and a golden monastery pagoda.

accessNotes: Dibrugarh Airport (60 km) / Naharkatia Railway Station (4 km)
openingHours: 08:00 - 17:00 daily (Monastery prayer times at dawn & dusk)
entryFee: Open village entry; homestay bookings directly with community hosts

name: Dehing Patkai National Park (Amazon of the East)
name_hi: Dehing Patkai National Park (Amazon of the East)
shortDescription: The Amazon of the East — Largest Lowland Tropical Rainforest in India
fullDescription: Spanning 231 sq km across the Patkai mountain foothills, Dehing Patkai is the largest contiguous stretch of lowland tropical wet evergreen rainforest in the Brahmaputra Valley. Its multi-tiered canopy is dominated by giant 50-meter Hollong trees (Dipterocarpus macrocarpus), Assam's State Tree. It is the only forest in the world confirmed to harbor seven species of wild cats (including the clouded leopard, marbled cat, and golden cat).
imageAttribution: Photo: Rituraj Dewan (CC BY-SA 4.0 via Wikimedia Commons)
accessNotes: Dibrugarh Airport (70 km) / Digboi Railway Station (18 km)
entryFee: Assam Forest Dept entry at Jeypore Range Office

name: Sualkuchi Silk Weavers Village
shortDescription: Manchester of Assam — Generational Handlooms of Certified Golden Muga Silk
fullDescription: Situated on the north bank of the Brahmaputra, Sualkuchi is celebrated as the 'Manchester of Assam'. It is the epicenter of Assam's GI-tagged Golden Muga Silk—an extraordinary golden filament produced exclusively in Assam by the semi-domesticated Antheraea assamensis silkworm, known for its natural golden sheen that intensifies with every wash. Walking through Sualkuchi, visitors hear the rhythmic clatter of over 25,000 wooden handlooms weaving Mekhela Sadors.
imageAttribution: Photo: Dhruba Jyoti Baruah (CC BY-SA 4.0 via Wikimedia Commons)
accessNotes: Guwahati City (35 km by road via Jalukbari and Saraighat Bridge)
entryFee: Free public access; cooperative weaver societies open daily

fullDescription: The Brahmaputra (meaning 'Son of Brahma') is the lifeblood and cultural spine of Assam. Boarding boutique expedition vessels (such as MV Mahabaahu or twilight river ferries from Guwahati), travelers cruise down the river to witness Gangetic river dolphins (Xihu) surfacing against molten gold sunsets, uninhabited sandy river islands, riverside wildlife buffer safaris, and stargazing bonfires on remote sandbanks.

name: Agnigarh Hillock & Tezpur Cultural City
shortDescription: Mythological Fortress of Fire & The City of Eternal Romance
fullDescription: Perched on a dramatic circular hillock overlooking the Brahmaputra, Agnigarh ('Fortress of Fire') is steeped in Hindu mythology. According to the Bhagavata Purana, King Banasura built this fortress surrounded by perpetual flames to isolate his daughter Princess Usha, where Prince Aniruddha (grandson of Lord Krishna) secretly courted her. Today, beautifully sculpted stone reliefs depicting the epic mythological war line the scenic winding pathways.
imageAttribution: Photo: Gitartha Bordoloi (CC BY-SA 3.0 via Wikimedia Commons)
accessNotes: Tezpur Airport (Salonibari - 10 km) / Guwahati (175 km)
entryFee: Tezpur Development Authority nominal entry ticket

name: Dibru-Saikhowa National Park & Maguri Beel
name_as: ডিব্ৰু-ছৈখোৱা ৰাষ্ট্ৰীয় উদ্যান আৰু মাগুৰী বিল
shortDescription: Flooded Island Wilderness, Feral Wild Horses & Gangetic River Dolphins
fullDescription: Encircled by the Brahmaputra, Lohit, and Dibru rivers in Upper Assam, Dibru-Saikhowa is one of the world's most unique flooded island national parks. Following the historic 1950 Assam earthquake, army horses left behind went wild and formed famous herds of feral horses that gallop along the sandbanks today. Adjoining Maguri-Motapung Beel is an internationally renowned wetland paradise for birdwatchers.

entryFee: Assam Forest Dept range counter at Guijan Ghat

name: Monabarie Tea Estate
shortDescription: Asia's Largest Contiguous Tea Estate (Established 1869 CE)
fullDescription: Covering over 1,158 hectares under tea cultivation along the lush north bank of the Brahmaputra in Biswanath district, Monabarie is renowned as the largest contiguous tea garden in Asia. Founded in 1869 by the British Assam Tea Company and currently managed by the McLeod Russel group, the garden features rolling verdant tea bushes, vintage British planter architecture, and expansive processing factories producing high-grade orthodox and CTC Assam teas.

bestSeason: October to April (Plucking season: May to October)
accessNotes: Tezpur Airport (75 km) / Biswanath Chariali Railway Station (8 km)
openingHours: Estate gates open 08:00 - 16:30 weekdays; prior permission for factory interior
entryFee: Complimentary entrance with prior notice to estate management office
highlights: Largest contiguous tea garden in Asia spanning 1,158 hectares
Colonial 19th-century planter heritage bungalows and club
Factory tours demonstrating CTC and orthodox tea rolling and fermentation
Scenic panoramic drive through emerald-green tea carpets

name: Cinnamara Historic Tea Estate & Maniram Dewan Memorial
name_as: চিনামৰা চাহ বাগিচা আৰু মণিৰাম দেৱান স্মৃতিসৌধ
shortDescription: First Indigenous Indian-Owned Tea Garden Founded in 1845 CE
fullDescription: Cinnamara holds monumental historical significance as the very first commercial tea plantation established by an indigenous Indian entrepreneur—the revered Assamese noble, statesman, and freedom fighter Maniram Dewan in 1845 CE. Rejecting the monopoly of the British Assam Company, Dewan pioneered native tea cultivation here. Located just south of Jorhat town, the estate preserves century-old tea bushes and the nearby historic memorial honoring Dewan's legacy in India's 1857 freedom uprising.

accessNotes: Jorhat Town Station (5 km) / Jorhat Rowriah Airport (10 km)
entryFee: Open heritage road access; factory visits by arrangement
highlights: First native Indian-owned tea garden in history (founded 1845)
Maniram Dewan memorial and historic tea heritage landmark
Adjoining Tocklai Tea Research Institute botanical collections
Tasting sessions of historic Upper Assam single-origin tea flushes

name: Guwahati Brahmaputra Riverfront Promenade & Ropeway
locality: Panbazar to Uzanbazar & North Guwahati Terminal
shortDescription: India's Longest River Ropeway (1.82 km) & Scenic Sunset Promenade
fullDescription: Spanning 1.82 kilometers directly across the mighty Brahmaputra river from Panbazar in Guwahati to Rajadwar in North Guwahati, this state-of-the-art passenger ropeway is India's longest river ropeway. Floating high above the azure river waters, the glass cabins offer breathtaking 360-degree aerial views of Peacock Island, Umananda temple, the Saraighat bridges, and Guwahati's verdant hilltops. The adjacent landscaped riverside promenade features walking tracks and sunset gazebos.

accessNotes: Guwahati Railway Station (1.5 km) / Kachari Ghat Terminal
entryFee: Ropeway tickets available at GMDA terminal counter; promenade access free

name: Kakochang Waterfalls & Karbi Hills Viewpoint
shortDescription: Magnificent Natural Waterfall Amidst Rubber & Coffee Plantations
fullDescription: Tucked inside the pristine forested hills of Karbi Anglong just 13 km from Bokakhat on the rim of Kaziranga, Kakochang is one of Assam's most picturesque natural waterfalls. Water cascades down craggy rock cliffs into a crystal-clear natural swimming pool, surrounded by dense evergreen subtropical canopies, aromatic coffee plantations, and rubber estates. It is also an exceptional vantage point for viewing the ruins of ancient Numaligarh.

bestSeason: October to April (Post-monsoon water volume is at its most spectacular)

openingHours: 07:00 - 16:30 daily (Daylight hours recommended for nature trek)
entryFee: Nominal local eco-development committee community maintenance fee

Ideal post-safari afternoon eco-excursion from Kaziranga

name: Panimur Waterfalls (Niagara of Assam)
shortDescription: Roaring Kopili River Cascades Celebrated as the Niagara of Assam
fullDescription: Carving its way through dramatic rocky limestone gorges in northwestern Dima Hasao, the turbulent Kopili River surges over massive stepped stone terraces at Panimur, earning it the moniker 'The Niagara of Assam'. Surrounded by untamed Barail hill forest tracts, the thunderous roaring falls create perpetual misty rainbows. Panimur is also a revered sacred pilgrimage spot for Dimasa and Karbi communities during the Magh Bihu full moon.

entryFee: Open nature access; local tourism committee parking fee applies
highlights: Stepped limestone river cascades creating thunderous foam and mist

name: Chandubi Lake & Garo Foothills Eco-Lagoon
shortDescription: Pristine Tectonic Lake Born from the Great 1897 Assam Earthquake
fullDescription: Located 64 km southwest of Guwahati at the foot of the Garo Hills, Chandubi Lake was naturally formed on June 12, 1897, when the catastrophic 8.1 magnitude Great Assam earthquake caused the forest basin to dramatically subside. The resulting 200-hectare freshwater lake is ringed by dense Sal and Teak forests and tranquil Rabha tribal villages. It is famed for its submerged forest roots, calm country boat paddling, and the vibrant annual Chandubi Festival in early January.

bestSeason: November to March (Chandubi Festival held every January)
accessNotes: Guwahati LGBI Airport (45 km) via Mirza-Chandubi Road
entryFee: Open nature access; boating tickets managed by Rabha Eco-Tourism Society
highlights: Natural tectonic earthquake lagoon with tranquil glassy waters
Traditional hand-paddled wooden canoe rides through submerged forests
Annual Chandubi Festival showcasing authentic Rabha folklore and crafts
Rich winter birding with migratory pintails, teals, and kingfishers
tagline: Pristine Tectonic Lake Born from the Great 1897 Assam Earthquake
description: Formed during the Great 1897 earthquake, Chandubi Lake is a pristine freshwater lagoon surrounded by Sal forests and Rabha villages.

name: Orang National Park (Mini Kaziranga)
locality: North Bank of Brahmaputra River, Silbori
shortDescription: Global Stronghold of One-Horned Rhinos & Royal Bengal Tigers
fullDescription: Often celebrated as the 'Mini Kaziranga' due to its identical landscape of alluvial grasslands, marshes, and riverine woodlands on the Brahmaputra's north bank, Orang covers 79 sq km and holds India's highest density of Royal Bengal Tigers. It also shelters over 125 Greater One-Horned Rhinos, wild elephants, critically endangered pygmy hogs, and rare Bengal Floricans.
imageAttribution: Photo: Diganta Talukdar (CC BY-SA 4.0 via Wikimedia Commons)
bestSeason: November to April (Closed during monsoon flood season)
accessNotes: Guwahati Airport (140 km) / Tezpur Airport (60 km) via NH 15
openingHours: 06:30 - 16:30 daily (Morning and afternoon jeep safari batches)
entryFee: Assam Forest Dept entry & vehicle safari tickets at Silbori Range Gate
highlights: Highest tiger density among northern Brahmaputra reserves
Over 125 Greater One-Horned Rhinos in compact alluvial grasslands

name: Deepor Beel Ramsar Wetland & Bird Sanctuary
shortDescription: Assam's Only Ramsar Wetland Site & Global Haven for Greater Adjutants
fullDescription: Located on the southwestern outskirts of Guwahati, Deepor Beel is a permanent freshwater lake and Assam's first designated Ramsar Site of international ecological importance. Covering 40 sq km, it forms a critical ecological corridor connecting Rani and Garbhanga reserve forests, with wild Asian elephant herds frequently bathing in its waters. International ornithologists flock here to observe over 200 bird species, including the world's largest concentration of the endangered Greater Adjutant Stork (Hargila).

name: Sri Surya Pahar Archaeological Complex
shortDescription: Sacred Hill of 99,999 Shiva Lingas & Ancient Interfaith Confluence
fullDescription: Rising 12 km southeast of Goalpara town, Sri Surya Pahar ('Hill of the Sun') is one of the most enigmatic archaeological treasures in Northeast India. According to local folklore, it was envisioned as a second Varanasi by King Banasura, with 99,999 monolithic stone Shiva Lingas sculpted across the granite slopes. Archaeological Survey of India (ASI) excavations have revealed rock-carved sun discs, votive stupas of Hinayana Buddhism dating to the 1st-2nd century BCE, and Jain Tirthankara figures (such as Adinatha), making it an extraordinary tri-religious sanctuary.

name: Madan Kamdev Archaeological Ruins (Khajuraho of Assam)
shortDescription: 10th–12th Century Kamarupa Pala Dynasty Sculpted Stone Temples
fullDescription: Perched atop Dewanagiri hillock overlooking the Madankuri river 40 km north of Guwahati, Madan Kamdev is renowned as the 'Khajuraho of Assam'. Built during the 10th to 12th century CE under the Kamarupa Pala dynasty, this archaeological complex preserves the ruins of 15 majestic stone temples. The granite and sandstone walls are embellished with exquisitely detailed erotic sculptures, celestial apsaras, griffins, and intricate friezes of Lord Shiva and Goddess Uma.

name: Sarthebari Bell-Metal Heritage Artisan Village
shortDescription: Centuries-Old Artisan Guild Hand-Forging GI-Tagged Bell-Metal Utensils
fullDescription: Located 90 km west of Guwahati in Barpeta district, Sarthebari is world-famous for its generational bell-metal (Kanh) industry—the second largest handicraft sector in Assam after handloom silk. Certified with a prestigious Geographical Indication (GI) tag, Sarthebari's master coppersmiths and braziers forge bronze and tin into ceremonial Xorai (Assam's cultural offering vessel), traditional dining plates (Kahi), water goblets (Kalah), and cymbals (Taal) entirely by hand over fiery open-hearth forges.

name: Asharikandi Terracotta & Pottery Craft Village
shortDescription: India's Premier Terracotta Cluster Famed for Handcrafted Hatima Dolls
fullDescription: Situated 14 km east of Dhubri town along the Gadadhar river, Asharikandi is the largest traditional terracotta and clay pottery cluster in India. Home to over 400 artisan families, the village is globally renowned for its unique 'Hatima Doll'—a mother figurine holding a child on her hip with elephant-shaped ears, sculpted entirely from special Hiramati alluvial clay found along riverbanks. Visitors walk through open courtyard kilns and observe pottery throwing on wooden wheels.
imageAttribution: Photo: Gitartha Bordoloi (CC BY-SA 3.0 via Wikimedia Commons)
bestSeason: October to March (Dry weather allows outdoor kiln firing)
accessNotes: Dhubri Railway Station (14 km) / Rupsi Airport (28 km)
entryFee: Free village walking access; pottery workshops offer hands-on clay moulding
highlights: Famous GI-heritage Hatima Terracotta Mother-Child craft
Traditional wood and straw-fired earthen kilns in courtyard clusters
Hands-on clay sculpting sessions guided by National Award-winning artisans
Direct artisan cooperative sales of eco-friendly home decor and toys
tagline: India's Premier Terracotta Cluster Famed for Handcrafted Hatima Dolls
description: Asharikandi is India's largest traditional terracotta craft village, world-renowned for its iconic handcrafted Hatima doll.

name: Latasil Bihu Cultural Stage & Rongali Bihu Grounds
name_as: লতাশিল বিহু সন্মিলন আৰু ৰঙালী বিহু মঞ্চ
shortDescription: Historic Birthplace of Urban Stage Bihu Celebrated Every April
fullDescription: Latasil Playground in Guwahati holds an iconic place in modern Assamese cultural history as the venue where the first urban stage Bihu (Bihu Mancha) was organized in 1952. Every year during mid-April (Assamese month of Bohaag), Latasil erupts into Assam's grandest Rongali Bihu festival, hosting thousands of spectators, traditional Dhol-Pepa players, and prestigious Bihu Rani and Bihu Kuwori folk dance championships under towering canopy stages.
imageAttribution: Traditional Assamese Bihu Folk Dance Celebration (CC BY-SA 4.0 by Edmonton Rongali Bihu via Wikimedia Commons)
bestSeason: Mid-April (Rongali Bihu / Bohaag Bihu festival week)
accessNotes: Guwahati Railway Station (2 km) / Panbazar Riverfront (1 km)
openingHours: Bihu festival evenings: 17:00 - midnight; Open sports grounds during daytime
entryFee: Complimentary open public admission to festival ground and stages
highlights: Assam's oldest historic urban Bihu stage (since 1952)
Traditional Pepa (buffalo horn flute), Dhol, and Gogona orchestral performances
Official Bihu Kuwori and Bihu Samragi classical dance pageants
Traditional Pitha, Laru, and Jolpan food festival stalls on festival perimeter
tagline: Historic Birthplace of Urban Stage Bihu Celebrated Every April
description: Latasil is the legendary birthplace of urban stage Bihu in Assam, hosting historic Rongali Bihu folk dance and music celebrations.

name: Majuli Raas Mahotsav Living Theatrical Festival
name_as: মাজুলীৰ ৰাস মহোৎসৱ আৰু ভাওনা সংস্কৃতি
name_hi: माजुली रास महोत्सव व भावना संस्कृति
shortDescription: 500-Year-Old Living Theatrical Celebration of Lord Krishna on the Island
fullDescription: Celebrated on the full moon night (Raas Purnima) of November, Majuli's Raas Mahotsav is one of the grandest open-air theatrical festivals in South Asia. Originating from Srimanta Sankardev's Neo-Vaishnavite Ankiya Nat tradition over 500 years ago, nearly every resident of the island transforms into an actor, musician, or artisan. Sattras and village Namghars mount dramatic enactments of Krishna's life with magnificent papier-mâché masks, Sattriya classical footwork, and Brajavali lyrics.
imageAttribution: Photo: Gitartha Bordoloi (CC BY-SA 3.0 via Wikimedia Commons)
accessNotes: Jorhat to Nimati Ghat (20 km) + Ferry to Majuli Kamalabari
openingHours: Performances run from 19:00 throughout the night across 60+ stages
entryFee: Open community entry; reserved seating passes available at Sattra desks
highlights: Over 60 simultaneous open-air theatrical stages operating all night
Spectacular traditional handcrafted bamboo and cow-dung masks
Authentic Classical Sattriya dance and Khol percussion orchestration
Island-wide community hospitality, clay-oven feasts, and temple illuminations
tagline: 500-Year-Old Living Theatrical Celebration of Lord Krishna on the Island
description: Majuli Raas Mahotsav is an extraordinary 500-year-old living island theater festival where monks and villagers perform Krishna's divine lila.

name_as: ঐতিহ্যবাহী অসমীয়া খাদ্য সংস্কৃতি আৰু থলুৱা সোৱাদ
name_hi: पारंपरिक असमिया पाक कला व थाली अनुभव
locality: Guwahati Heritage Zone & Jorhat Planters Guild
shortDescription: Slow-Cooked Khar, Masor Tenga, Bamboo Shoot & Fragrant Joha Rice
fullDescription: Assam's culinary heritage is defined by fresh river produce, wild indigenous herbs (Xaak), slow wood-fire cooking, and subtle, natural flavors free of heavy spices. A curated Assamese Thali journey begins with Omita Khar (papaya alkali palate purifier), continues to fresh Rohu or Chitol Masor Tenga (tart fish curry infused with Outenga elephant apple or Thekera), smoked meats in bamboo tubes (Khorika), Duck cooked with Ash Gourd (Kumura), and culminates in aromatic Joha rice, fermented bamboo shoots (Khorisa), and sticky Bora rice payash.
imageAttribution: Authentic Assamese Fish Thali in Dibrugarh (CC BY-SA 4.0 by Subhashish Panigrahi via Wikimedia Commons)
bestSeason: Year-round (Winter season features fresh mustard greens and duck delicacies)
accessNotes: Guwahati Central City & Jorhat Heritage Dining circuits
entryFee: Dining per order; verified heritage restaurants listed on state tourism portal
highlights: Authentic Bell-Metal Thali service honoring 600-year Ahom royal gastronomy
Khar & Tenga: distinctive alkali and sour flavor spectrum unique to Assam
Organic wild foraging: Dhekia Xaak (fiddlehead fern), Manimuni, and Bhedailota
Indigenous fermented dips: Khorisa (bamboo shoot) and Bhut Jolokia chillies
tagline: Slow-Cooked Khar, Masor Tenga, Bamboo Shoot & Fragrant Joha Rice
description: Experience authentic Assamese culinary traditions served on pure bell-metal thalis featuring Khar, Masor Tenga, and Joha rice.

name: Mishing Chang-Ghar Traditional Kitchen & Cultural Trail
name_as: মিচিং চাংঘৰৰ ৰন্ধনশালা আৰু আপং সংস্কৃতি
name_hi: मिशिंग चांग-घर पारंपरिक रसोई व संस्कृति
shortDescription: Bamboo-Tube Smoked Fish, Namsing, Wild Herbs & Traditional Rice Brews
fullDescription: The Mishing community—one of the largest indigenous riverine tribes of Assam—possesses an extraordinary gastronomic tradition developed over centuries along the Brahmaputra floodplains. Built atop elevated Chang-Ghar (bamboo stilt houses) to adapt to river tides, the kitchen fire (Meram) burns continually. Specialties include Namsing (sun-dried ground fish with herbs), smoked pork roasted in hollow green bamboo (Khorika), fish wrapped in banana leaves (Patot Diya), and ceremonial fermented rice wine (Nogin Apong and Po:ro Apong).
imageAttribution: Traditional Chang Ghar Stilt Architecture of the Mising Community (CC BY-SA 4.0 by Homen Hazarika via Wikimedia Commons)
bestSeason: October to April (Special: Ali-Aye-Ligang spring harvest festival in February)
accessNotes: Nimati Ghat to Kamalabari Ferry + 25-minute drive to Jengraimukh
openingHours: 10:00 - 18:00 daily (Homestay culinary experiences with prior arrangement)
entryFee: Community culinary homestay dining per booking
highlights: Stilt house Chang-Ghar kitchen experience around the central hearth (Meram)
Traditional fish roasted inside fresh green bamboo stalks over wood embers
Authentic Po:ro Apong (dark sweet rice brew fermented with 40+ medicinal herbs)
Ali-Aye-Ligang folk dance and harvest food festival in mid-February
tagline: Bamboo-Tube Smoked Fish, Namsing, Wild Herbs & Traditional Rice Brews
description: Authentic indigenous riverine cuisine in traditional stilt houses, featuring bamboo-tube roasted fish and ceremonial herb-fermented rice brew.

name_as: অসম ৰাজ্যিক চিৰিয়াখানা আৰু উদ্ভিদ উদ্যান
name_hi: असम राज्य चिड़ियाघर व वानस्पतिक उद्यान
locality: Hengrabari Reserve Forest, R.G. Baruah Road, Guwahati
shortDescription: 432-Acre Green Lung of Guwahati Conserving 500+ Rare Orchid & Tree Species
fullDescription: Sprawled over 432 acres (175 hectares) of undulating green hills within the protected Hengrabari Reserve Forest right in the heart of Guwahati, the Assam State Zoo-cum-Botanical Garden is the largest green lung of the capital city. Established in 1957, the botanical division preserves a vast herbarium, indigenous bamboo arboretum, medicinal plant conservation groves, and a specialized Orchidarium sheltering rare Northeast Indian wild orchids (such as Rhynchostylis retusa, the Kopou Phool).
imageAttribution: Assam State Zoo cum Botanical Garden, Guwahati (CC BY-SA 4.0 by Tridiv Bordoloi via Wikimedia Commons)
bestSeason: October to April (Orchid blooming season: March to May)
accessNotes: Guwahati Railway Station (6 km) / Lokpriya Gopinath Bordoloi Airport (26 km)
entryFee: Official Forest Dept counter ticket & online booking at assamstatezoo.in
highlights: 432 acres of pristine reserve forest canopy in the heart of Guwahati
Specialized botanical Orchid House showcasing rare indigenous species
Endangered one-horned rhino and Golden Langur conservation breeding centers
Shaded hill nature trails and tranquil central lake with waterbirds
tagline: 432-Acre Green Lung of Guwahati Conserving 500+ Rare Orchid & Tree Species
description: Spread across 432 acres of reserve forest, this botanical garden and conservation zoo is Guwahati's premier green biodiversity sanctuary.

name_hi: बगामाटी इको-पार्क व बोरनदी हरित स्थल
shortDescription: White-Stone Riverbed, Hanging Footbridge & Himalayan Foothill Pine Groves
fullDescription: Located right on the border of Assam and Bhutan in Baksa district, Bogamati ('White Soil / White Sand') is a picturesque green eco-destination created where the Bornadi river flows down from the Bhutanese hills. Famous for its bright white river gravel bed, panoramic pine-covered mountain vistas, and a 200-meter suspension hanging footbridge over the clear turquoise waters, it features landscaped green eco-parks, gentle river rafting, and scenic nature walking promenades.
imageAttribution: Bogamati Scenic Eco Park and Bornadi River, Baksa (CC BY-SA 4.0 by Jugal Barman via Wikimedia Commons)
bestSeason: November to April (Crisp mountain air and tranquil river currents)
accessNotes: Rangiya Junction (40 km) / Guwahati City (90 km via Baihata-Goreswar road)
openingHours: 07:00 - 17:00 daily (Daylight hours strictly enforced near border)
entryFee: Nominal local Bodoland Eco-Tourism Society green maintenance pass
highlights: Scenic suspension footbridge across the Bornadi River gorge
Picturesque picnic and eco-walking groves against Bhutan mountain ridges
Gentle white-water rubber boat rafting and zip-line adventure
Golden Buddha statue atop the hill offering 360-degree valley vistas
tagline: White-Stone Riverbed, Hanging Footbridge & Himalayan Foothill Pine Groves
description: Nestled along the Bornadi River on the Bhutan border, Bogamati is an eco-park destination famed for white gravel riverbeds and pine hills.

shortDescription: Multi-Day Road Itinerary: 600-Year Ahom Capitals, Rain Forests & Planter Mansions
fullDescription: This comprehensive scenic travel guide links the royal heartland of Assam across Sivasagar, Charaideo, and Dibrugarh districts. The 4-day curated itinerary commences at Asia's oldest royal amphitheater (Rang Ghar) and the underground Talatal Ghar in Sivasagar, journeys to the UNESCO World Heritage royal pyramid mounds of Charaideo (inscribed 2024), navigates through the lowland tropical rainforest of Dehing Patkai, and concludes among the historic colonial tea bungalows and golf courses of Dibrugarh.

fullDescription: Encircled by emerald hill ranges in southern Assam, the Barak Valley offers an enchanting alternative travel circuit. This scenic guide covers the historic 17th-century Khaspur palace ruins (the final royal seat of the Dimasa Kachari kingdom featuring Dimasa brick arches and the Lion Gate), peaceful tea garden expanses along the lush Chatachura ranges, the historic Badarpur Mughal-British river fort, and sunset boat journeys on the placid Barak River.

bestSeason: October to March (Crisp pleasant winter conditions)
accessNotes: Silchar Airport (Kumbhirgram) / Silchar Railway Station (Broad gauge connectivity)
openingHours: Monuments open 09:00 - 17:00; Scenic highway driving during daylight
entryFee: State Archaeology Department nominal site fees at Khaspur
highlights: Khaspur Dimasa Kingdom royal brick palaces and monumental Lion Gate (1706 CE)
Uncrowded century-old tea estates set among rolling undulating valleys
Scenic hill transit via scenic Vistadome train through Barail mountain tunnels
Authentic Sylheti and Dimasa culinary traditions and handloom weavers

shortDescription: Golden Langurs, Virgin Himalayan Reserves & Rich Bodo Handloom Culture
fullDescription: Extending across the Bodoland Territorial Region (BTR) in northwestern Assam, this scenic guide traverses the southern foothills of Bhutan. The route integrates Raimona National Park (Assam's 6th National Park, famed for rare Golden Langurs and butterfly diversity), the UNESCO World Heritage natural paradise of Manas, community-managed ecotourism camps in Bansbari, and authentic Dokhona handloom weaving cooperatives in Kokrajhar.

accessNotes: New Bongaigaon Junction (Main rail transit) / Kokrajhar Railway Station
entryFee: BTR Forest Department entry passes at respective national park range gates
highlights: Twin national park wildlife circuit (Manas + Raimona National Parks)
Dedicated habitat of endangered Golden Langurs in Ripu-Chirang reserve forests
Traditional Bodo homestays featuring local music (Kham, Sifung) and organic feasts
Indigenous handloom weaving workshops producing authentic Dokhona and Aronai

name: Pari Hareswar Devalaya
shortDescription: Ancient Shiva Temple & Origin of Classical Devadasi Dance Heritage
fullDescription: Pari Hareswar Devalaya at Dubi near Pathsala is an ancient and revered Shiva shrine dating back to early Kamarupa rulers. The temple is historically renowned for its preserved traditions of Devadasi nritya (classical temple dance). Copper-plate charters of King Bhaskaravarman discovered here affirm the temple's antiquity and profound spiritual significance in Assamese cultural history.

bestSeason: October to April (Magnificent during Maha Shivaratri)
accessNotes: Pathsala Railway Station (4 km) / Lokpriya Gopinath Bordoloi Airport Guwahati (95 km)
entryFee: Free / Open for prayer and cultural exploration

name: Pathsala Mobile Theatre Cultural Hub
shortDescription: The Heartland of Assam's Unique Mobile Theatre (Bhramyoman) Tradition
fullDescription: Pathsala in Bajali district is celebrated as the cultural crucible of Assam's world-renowned Mobile Theatre ('Bhramyoman Natyadal') industry. Pioneers like Achyut Lahkar founded Nataraj Theatre here in 1963, blending grand mobile sets, live orchestras, Hollywood-scale stage mechanics, and indigenous Assamese drama. Visiting Pathsala during rehearsal seasons (August–September) and festive performances offers an authentic immersion into living Assamese performing arts.

bestSeason: August to March (Peak rehearsal & touring season)

name: Kakoijana Golden Langur Sanctuary
shortDescription: Global Habitat and Community Conservation Stronghold of the Rare Golden Langur
fullDescription: Spanning over 17 sq km of semi-evergreen and moist deciduous forests, Kakoijana Reserve Forest is internationally acclaimed for harboring one of the densest populations of the endangered Golden Langur (Trachypithecus geei). Through pioneering community conservation partnerships with local villagers, the forest shelters over 500 golden langurs, hornbills, leopard cats, and rare butterfly species.
imageAttribution: Photo: Golden Langur (Trachypithecus geei) in Assam (CC BY-SA 3.0 via Wikimedia Commons)
accessNotes: New Bongaigaon Junction (15 km) / Guwahati Airport (155 km)
entryFee: Forest entry permit applicable at Range Office

name: Jogighopa Rock-Cut Caves & Monoliths
shortDescription: Ancient 5th–8th Century Salasthambha Monolithic Cave Architecture on the Brahmaputra
fullDescription: Perched dramatically along the red rocky bluffs overlooking the mighty Brahmaputra, the Rock-Cut Caves of Jogighopa represent unique monolithic stone architectural monuments dating back to the Salasthambha period (approx. 5th to 8th century AD). The caves served as meditative viharas and hermitages for ancient ascetics. Nearby hillocks preserve ancient stone carvings, chiseled steps, and sweeping vistas of the Naranarayan Setu bridge.
imageAttribution: Photo: Jogighopa overlooking Brahmaputra (CC BY-SA 4.0 via Wikimedia Commons)
accessNotes: Jogighopa Station / New Bongaigaon Junction (32 km)
entryFee: Free / Protected Archaeological Site
tagline: Ancient 5th–8th Century Salasthambha Monolithic Cave Architecture
description: Perched dramatically along the red rocky bluffs overlooking the mighty Brahmaputra, the Rock-Cut Caves of Jogighopa represent unique monolithic stone architectural monuments dating back to the Salasthambha period.
highlights: Five cubical monolithic stone-hewn meditation chambers
Panoramic views of the Brahmaputra River and Naranarayan Setu

name: Akashiganga Waterfalls & Ancient Shrine
shortDescription: Sacred Forest Cascades and Kalika Purana Historical Archaeological Site
fullDescription: Nestled in the lush evergreen foothills between Hojai and Karbi Anglong, Akashiganga is a spectacular natural waterfall associated with the ancient Kalika Purana. According to legend, sacred drops from Goddess Sati fell here, creating a perennial stream that plunges down a sheer rocky gorge. Archaeological explorations around the falls have uncovered 10th-12th century stone pillars, carvings, and historic temple plinths.

shortDescription: Dense Sal Forest, Wild Elephant Corridors and Diverse Avian Sanctuary
fullDescription: Doboka Reserve Forest encompasses an important wildlife refuge in central Assam. Dominated by majestic sal and teak canopies, the forest forms a crucial migratory corridor for Asian elephants and shelters barking deer, leopards, and over 150 species of resident and migratory birds.

name: Billeshwar Devalaya (Belsor)
shortDescription: Ancient 500-Year-Old Historic Shiva Temple Rebuilt by Ahom King Shiva Singha
fullDescription: Billeshwar Devalaya at Belsor, about 14 km from Nalbari town, is one of the most prominent historic Shiva temples in Lower Assam. Believed to date originally back to the Kamarupa epoch, it was reconstructed with magnificent brick masonry by Ahom Swargadeo Shiva Singha in the early 18th century. The temple houses an ancient Shiva lingam and is famous for its grand annual Maha Shivaratri festival.

accessNotes: Nalbari Railway Station (14 km) / Guwahati (65 km)
entryFee: Free entry / Open to all pilgrims and visitors

shortDescription: The Epicenter of the Celebrated 13-Day Historic Nalbari Raas Mahotsav
fullDescription: Nalbari Sri Sri Hari Mandir, founded in 1931, is the cultural heart of Nalbari. The temple complex is nationally renowned for hosting the glorious 13-day Nalbari Raas Mahotsav every autumn during Raas Purnima. The festival transforms the entire town with hundreds of handcrafted animated clay clay idols depicting Lord Krishna's lila, traditional melas, and vibrant theatrical performances.

entryFee: Free / Open public celebration

shortDescription: Historic Border Hilltop Shakti Shrine Overlooking Bangladesh Floodplains
fullDescription: Situated atop an elevated hillock in Mankachar near the international Indo-Bangladesh border, this sacred Kamakhya Temple dates back centuries. The temple offers magnificent panoramic views of the Brahmaputra alluvial basin and neighboring Garo Hills. Pilgrims from all around the tri-junction of Assam, Meghalaya, and Bangladesh gather here during annual Navaratri and Ambubachi celebrations.

name: Mir Jumla Historic Tomb & Cannon Post
shortDescription: 1663 Monument of Mughal General Mir Jumla on the Historic Route to Assam
fullDescription: Located at Thakuranbari near Mankachar, this historic site marks the tomb of Mir Jumla (Muazzam Khan), the celebrated Mughal Subahdar of Bengal who led the 1662 Mughal invasion of Assam. Stricken with illness on his return retreat from Garhgaon, he died here in March 1663. The historic brick monument and adjacent old cannon posts provide an extraordinary window into medieval Assamese and Mughal military history.

entryFee: Free / State Protected Heritage Site

shortDescription: Centuries-Old Historic Winter Trade Fair and Cultural Confluence with Bhutan
fullDescription: Daranga Mela, situated right along the international border with Samdrup Jongkhar (Bhutan), is one of the oldest winter trade and cultural confluences in Eastern India. For centuries, Bhutanese highlanders descend to Daranga during the winter months to trade woolens, mountain spices, musk, and traditional handicrafts with Assamese and Bodo merchants.

name: Bhairabkunda Scenic River Confluence
shortDescription: Spectacular Tri-Junction of Assam, Bhutan, and Arunachal Pradesh on the Dhansiri
fullDescription: Bhairabkunda is an awe-inspiring geographical wonder located at the tri-junction where the borders of Assam, Bhutan, and Arunachal Pradesh meet. Here, the glacial Himalayan rivers Jampui and Bhairabi merge to form the Dhansiri River against a panoramic wall of jagged green peaks. Renowned as a premier eco-tourism and winter picnic destination, Bhairabkunda features an ancient Shiva temple, ropeways, suspension bridges, and forested islands.

name: Bornadi Wildlife Sanctuary
shortDescription: Protected Foothills Refuge of the Critically Endangered Pygmy Hog and Hispid Hare
fullDescription: Spanning 26.22 sq km at the foothills of the Himalayas, Bornadi Wildlife Sanctuary was specially notified to preserve the critically endangered Pygmy Hog (Porcula salvania) and Hispid Hare (Caprolagus hispidus). The sanctuary blends sub-Himalayan bhabar grasslands with moist deciduous sal forests, harboring Asian elephants, leopards, peafowl, and Himalayan black bears.

name: Khanduli Highland Meadows & Tourist Village
shortDescription: Breathtaking Rolling Green Hilltop Meadows on the Assam-Meghalaya Plateau
fullDescription: Khanduli is a picturesque highland plateau situated in West Karbi Anglong along the border with Meghalaya. The landscape features rolling green grassy hills reminiscent of European countryside, dotted with pine clusters and traditional Karbi tribal villages. The cool year-round climate and mist-clad valleys make Khanduli one of Assam's most refreshing, unexplored eco-tourism frontiers.

name: Barpeta Satra & Kirtan Ghar
shortDescription: Historic 1583 AD Vaishnavite Monastery Established by Mahapurusha Madhabdeva
fullDescription: Barpeta Satra, founded by Sri Sri Madhabdeva in 1583 AD, is one of the most venerated seats of Ekasarana Dharma in Assam. Known affectionately as the 'Barpeta Than', its monumental Kirtan Ghar features grand wood-carved pillars, ornate ceiling frescoes, and traditional brass oil-lamps kept continuously burning. The satra is globally famous for its vibrant Doul Utsav (Holi) celebration, where thousands play phaguguri (colored powder) to traditional holigeet hymns.

bestSeason: October to April (Magnificent during Doul Utsav / Holi)

entryFee: Free / Open for prayer and cultural exploration

name: Biswanath Ghat (Gupta Kashi)
shortDescription: UNESCO Tentative Heritage Riverfront, Submerged Shiva Temple and Historic Stone Ghats
fullDescription: Biswanath Ghat, reverently called 'Gupta Kashi' (Hidden Varanasi), is a breathtaking historical pilgrimage riverbank on the Brahmaputra in Biswanath district. Awarded the Best Tourism Village of India in 2023, it features an ancient submerged Shiva temple whose stone shikhara emerges from the river during low-water winter months, ancient Ahom-era stone embankments, and scenic view of Kaziranga's northern shores.

name: Khaspur Ancient Kachari Royal Palace Ruins
shortDescription: 18th-Century Historic Brick Capital Ruins of the Dimasa Kachari Kingdom
fullDescription: Khaspur, located 20 km from Silchar in Cachar district, served as the last capital of the Dimasa Kachari kingdom after their retreat from Maibang. Dating to the reign of King Tamradhwaj Narayan in the early 18th century, the archaeological complex preserves royal brick monuments including the grand Lion Gate (Singha Dwar), Sun Gate, Snan Mandir (Royal Bath), and ancient temple plinths.

name: Batadrava Than (Bordowa)
shortDescription: Sacred Birthplace of Mahapurusha Srimanta Sankaradeva & Birthplace of Neo-Vaishnavism
fullDescription: Batadrava Than at Bordowa in Nagaon district is the holy birthplace of Srimanta Sankaradeva (1449–1568 AD), the saint, social reformer, playwright, and polymath who unified Assam through the Bhakti movement. Established by Sankaradeva at the age of nineteen in 1468 AD, it houses the first sacred Kirtan Ghar, the ancient Silikha tree under which the saint composed devotional classics, and the holy Akashiganga pond.

bestSeason: Throughout the year (Especially during Sankaradeva Tithi and Doul Utsav)

entryFee: Free / Open to all pilgrims and visitors

fullDescription: Kalamati is a dramatic, offbeat eco-tourism destination situated in Chirang adjacent to the Panbari Range of Manas. The location offers exhilarating views of undisturbed Himalayan forests.

name: Gerukamukh Subansiri River Gorge
shortDescription: Spectacular Deep Mountain River Gorge of the Gold-Bearing Subansiri River
fullDescription: Gerukamukh is a breathtaking scenic canyon where the mighty Subansiri ('River of Gold') bursts through the towering Himalayan foothills into the plains of Upper Assam. Surrounded by emerald jungle-clad mountains, dramatic limestone cliffs, and crystal azure pools, Gerukamukh is a paradise for nature photographers, anglers in pursuit of the Golden Mahseer, and river campers.

bestSeason: October to April (Magnificent winter blue river waters)

entryFee: Free public access

name: Ghuguha Dol & Royal Ahom Monument
shortDescription: Historic 17th-Century Ahom Royal Temple Dedicated to Queen Jayamati
fullDescription: Ghuguha Dol is an important protected historic monument located in Dhemaji district. Built during the reign of Ahom Swargadeo Rudra Singha in memory of Queen Mother Jayamati, this ancient brick dol stands beside a grand historic royal tank (Pukhuri). The surrounding area is steeped in folklore and serves as an important archaeological showcase of Ahom architecture on the north bank.

name: Siddheswar Temple & Kapila Muni Hermitage
shortDescription: Ancient Sacred Shiva Shrine on the Barak Riverbanks Associated with Sage Kapila
fullDescription: Siddheswar Temple is one of the most sacred and ancient spiritual sanctuaries in the Barak Valley, situated along the tranquil river bend of the Barak at Badarpurghat in Hailakandi. Believed to have been originally sanctified by Sage Kapila Muni, the temple is home to a swayambhu Shiva lingam and is the centerpiece of the grand annual Baruni Mela, where tens of thousands take holy dips in the river.

bestSeason: October to April (Magnificent during Baruni Snan Mela)

entryFee: Free / Open to all pilgrims

name: Pachbhai Lake & Tea Estate Trails
shortDescription: Picturesque Wetland Lake Surrounded by Rolling Green Hillocks of Tea
fullDescription: Pachbhai Lake near Lala in Hailakandi district is a serene ecological wetland framed by rolling green tillas (tea hillocks) of southern Assam. The lake attracts numerous migratory ducks, whistling teals, and kingfishers during the winter months, while the adjacent heritage tea estates provide scenic walks and traditional tea-tasting experiences.

name: Kangthilangso Waterfalls & Eco Trail
shortDescription: Spectacular Multi-Tiered Jungle Waterfalls Hidden in the Karbi Hills
fullDescription: Kangthilangso is one of Assam's most breathtaking natural waterfalls, tucked away amidst dense tropical semi-evergreen rainforests in Karbi Anglong district. The waterfall plunges over multiple wide granite steps, forming deep turquoise pools framed by ancient moss-covered tree ferns and jungle vines. An eco-trek through indigenous Karbi villages leads visitors to this pristine cascading paradise.

name_hi: गरमपानी अभयारण्य एवं गर्म पानी के सोते
shortDescription: Centuries-Old Geothermal Sulphur Springs and Hoolock Gibbon Sanctuary
fullDescription: Garampani, meaning 'hot water', is one of the oldest wildlife sanctuaries in Assam, covering 6.05 sq km of tropical dense canopy. Famous for its natural geothermal hot sulphur springs which are believed to have therapeutic medicinal properties, the sanctuary is also an essential habitat for India's only ape species, the Hoolock Gibbon, as well as capped langurs, elephants, and hornbills.

name_as: সোণ বিল জলাশয় আৰু পক্ষী অভয়াৰণ্য
shortDescription: Asia's Second Largest Seasonal Wetland Lake and Migratory Waterfowl Paradise
fullDescription: Son Beel in Karimganj district is the largest wetland in Assam and the second largest seasonal lake in Asia. During monsoon months, Son Beel transforms into a vast inland sea, while in dry winter months it converts into emerald green fertile rice paddies with shallow winding waterways. Hijol trees (Barringtonia acutangula) stand half-submerged in the shimmering waters, creating an ethereal spectacle for photographers and birdwatchers.

entryFee: Free / Country boat hire available from local fishermen

name: Badarpur Fort (Barak Riverfront)
shortDescription: 18th-Century Strategic Stone Fort on the Banks of the Barak River
fullDescription: Badarpur Fort is a significant historical fortification constructed along the northern bank of the Barak River in Karimganj district. Built strategically by the British East India Company in the late 18th century to monitor river trade and repel Burmese invasions, the stone battlements, arched cannon embrasures, and river sentry bastions remain remarkably preserved amidst tranquil riverside gardens.

entryFee: Free / Protected Archaeological Site

name: Barpeta Doul Mandir & Historic Doul Utsav
name_as: বৰপেটা সত্ৰৰ দৌল মন্দিৰ আৰু মহা দৌল উৎসৱ (হোলী)
name_hi: बरपेटा दौल मंदिर एवं दौल उत्सव (होली)
shortDescription: The Iconic 7-Tiered Hepta-Pyramidal Temple of Kalia Thakur and Grand 5-Day Spring Doul Utsav
fullDescription: The Doul Mandir at Barpeta Satra is a masterpiece of indigenous Assamese wooden and brick architecture. Featuring a unique seven-tiered (Sat-Tahala) pyramidal design, this historic sanctum was erected in the late 16th century by Sri Sri Mathuradas Burha Ata, the first Satradhikar appointed by Madhabdeva. During the spring Phalguna Purnima (Holi), the Doul Mandir becomes the focal point of the world-famous Barpeta Doul Utsav. The festival begins with Gondh (sacred bonfire), followed by Bhor Doul, and concludes with the spectacular 'Suwori' (Phakuwa), where thousands of devotees clad in traditional white dhotis and gamusas chant devotional Holigeet and shower Phaguguri (red fragrant powder) in celestial ecstasy.
imageAttribution: Photo: Celebrating Doul Utsav (Holi) at Barpeta Satra (CC BY-SA 4.0 via Wikimedia Commons)
bestSeason: March (During Doul Utsav / Phalguna Purnima) to April
accessNotes: Barpeta Road Railway Station (21 km) / LGBI Airport Guwahati (98 km) / NH 27
openingHours: 05:00 - 20:00 daily (Open all night during active Doul Utsav days)
entryFee: Free / Open to all devotees and visitors (Footwear prohibited within sanctum)
tagline: The Iconic 7-Tiered Hepta-Pyramidal Temple of Kalia Thakur and Grand 5-Day Spring Doul Utsav
description: The Doul Mandir at Barpeta Satra is a masterpiece of indigenous Assamese wooden and brick architecture, featuring a unique seven-tiered pyramidal design where Kalia Thakur is brought during Doul Yatra.
highlights: Architectural wonder: 7-tiered (Sat-Tahala) wooden pagoda temple constructed for Lord Krishna (Govinda)
The sacred bonfire of Gondh and ritual circumambulation (Doul Ghuran) around the Math
Soulful chorus singing of traditional Holigeet and Borgeet composed by Madhabdeva and Harideva
The grand finale 'Suwori' ritual where devotees joyously toss aromatic red Phaguguri into the skies
Devotees breaking bamboo blockades (Bansh Bhanga) at Kanheli Gate in ceremonial homecoming

entry_permit: Free entry / Open to all pilgrims and cultural tourists

name: Kareng Ghar (Garhgaon Royal Palace)
shortDescription: Magnificent seven-storied royal palace of the Ahom Kingdom featuring indigenous brick and organic mortar architecture.
fullDescription: Kareng Ghar, also known as the Garhgaon Palace, was the official capital palace of the Tai-Ahom dynasty. Originally commissioned in 1540 by King Suklenmung and later rebuilt in brick and stone with indigenous mortar made of sticky Bora rice, duck eggs, and pulse flour by King Rajeshwar Singha in 1752, this four-storied structure (with subterranean chambers) represents the zenith of secular Ahom royal architecture. Surrounded by defensive moats and green maidans, it remains a premier protected monument of the Archaeological Survey of India.
imageAttribution: Photo: Royal Palace of Garhgaon (CC BY-SA 4.0 via Wikimedia Commons)
accessNotes: Located in Garhgaon, 15 km from Sivasagar town and 13 km from Sonari. Well-connected by ASTC buses and auto-rickshaws along the Sivasagar-Nazira road.
entryFee: ₹25 (Indians), ₹300 (Foreign Nationals)

name: Da-Parbatia Archaeological Ruins
shortDescription: Ancient 5th-century Gupta-era doorframe ruins representing the oldest surviving stone sculpture in Assam.
fullDescription: Da-Parbatia is one of the oldest archaeological sites in Assam, located just outside Tezpur. The main highlight is the breathtaking stone doorframe of a temple dating back to the 5th-6th century Gupta period, featuring exquisitely carved river goddesses Ganga and Yamuna standing on lotus pedestals accompanied by celestial attendants. The site also contains brick foundation plinths of an Ahom-era Shiva temple built on top of the ancient Gupta sanctuary.
imageAttribution: Photo: 5th-century Gupta Doorframe of Da-Parbatia (CC BY-SA 4.0 via Wikimedia Commons)
accessNotes: Located 5 km west of Tezpur city centre. Easily reached via auto-rickshaw or taxi.
entryFee: Free Entry (Protected National Monument)

name: Ambari Archaeological Site & Museum
shortDescription: Remarkable urban archaeological excavation site revealing ancient Kamarupa sculptural studios and medieval brick structures.
fullDescription: Accidentally unearthed in 1969 in the heart of Guwahati city, Ambari is a vital archaeological window into the art and trade of ancient Kamarupa from the 7th to the 13th centuries CE. Excavations revealed a major workshop for stone sculptors and artists producing stunning icons of Surya, Vishnu, Ganga, and Nataraja, along with Roman and Chinese pottery fragments proving international maritime trade connections along the Brahmaputra.
imageAttribution: Photo: Ambari Medieval Sculptural Excavation (CC BY-SA 4.0 via Wikimedia Commons)
accessNotes: Situated on GNB Road in Uzan Bazar, near Guwahati Club and Dighalipukhuri. Within walking distance from Guwahati Railway Station (1 km).
entryFee: ₹20 (Adults), ₹10 (Students)

name: Digboi Centenary Oil Museum & Heritage Area
name_as: ডিগবৈ তেল যাদুঘৰ আৰু ঐতিহ্য ক্ষেত্ৰ
shortDescription: Birthplace of the modern petroleum industry in Asia, featuring the historic Well No. 1 and an open-air machinery museum.
fullDescription: Digboi is the birthplace of the Indian and Asian petroleum industry, where crude oil was first drilled in 1889 following the legendary elephant trail discovery. The Digboi Centenary Oil Museum, established near the original Discovery Well No. 1, showcases antique steam locomotives, vintage drilling rigs, colonial-era bungalows, and the century-old refinery that remains operational to this day.
imageAttribution: Photo: Historic Digboi Oil Well No. 1 (CC BY-SA 4.0 via Wikimedia Commons)
accessNotes: Located in Digboi town, 35 km from Tinsukia along NH-38. Well connected by rail and highway from Dibrugarh Airport (80 km).
entryFee: ₹50 (Adults), ₹20 (Students)

name: Navagraha Temple (Chitrachal Hill)
shortDescription: Ancient astronomical temple dedicated to the nine celestial bodies, built atop Chitrachal Hill by Ahom King Rajeswar Singha.
fullDescription: Perched atop Chitrachal Hill (Navagraha Hill) in south-eastern Guwahati, the Navagraha Temple is an ancient center of astronomical and astrological study. Rebuilt in 1752 by Ahom King Rajeswar Singha, the sanctum sanctorum enshrines nine Shiva Lingas representing the nine celestial planets (Surya, Chandra, Mangala, Budha, Brihaspati, Shukra, Shani, Rahu, and Ketu), each draped in distinct colored silk cloths.
imageAttribution: Photo: Historic Navagraha Temple of Guwahati (CC BY-SA 4.0 via Wikimedia Commons)
accessNotes: Accessible via motorable hilltop road from Silpukhuri or Chenikuthi. Taxi and auto-rickshaws go directly to temple gates.
entryFee: Free Entry

name: Basistha Ashram & Historic Cave Temple
shortDescription: Serene Vedic hermitage of Sage Basistha set amidst the confluence of three mountain streams in the lush southern hills.
fullDescription: Basistha Ashram is a legendary pilgrimage site situated on the southern fringes of Guwahati, at the meeting point of three pristine mountain rivulets—Sandhya, Lalita, and Kanta. Believed to have been the hermitage of the Vedic sage Basistha, the existing brick temple was constructed by Ahom King Rajeswar Singha in the mid-18th century. Surrounded by dense reserve forest and soothing waterfalls, it offers a peaceful spiritual retreat.
imageAttribution: Photo: Basistha Temple & Stream (CC BY-SA 4.0 via Wikimedia Commons)
accessNotes: Located at the terminus of Basistha Road, 12 km from Guwahati Railway Station. Regular city bus and taxi service available.

name: Aswaklanta Historic Temple (North Guwahati)
shortDescription: Historic riverside temple overlooking the Brahmaputra, built in 1720 CE by Ahom King Siva Singha.
fullDescription: Aswaklanta Temple is an exquisite riverside shrine on the northern bank of the Brahmaputra in North Guwahati. According to folklore, Lord Krishna rested his horses here while on his way from Kundina to Dwarka. Constructed by Ahom King Siva Singha in 1720 CE, the complex comprises two shrines—Bar Aswaklanta on the rocky hill slope and Chhota Aswaklanta near the water’s edge—adorned with delicate stone sculptures of Dashavatara.

name: Doul Govinda Temple & Holi Pilgrimage
shortDescription: Renowned Krishna temple famous for its vibrant 5-day Doul Utsav (Holi) celebration and scenic riverside ghats.
fullDescription: Situated in Rajaduar on the foot of Chandrabharati hill in North Guwahati, Sri Sri Doul Govinda Temple is one of the most revered Krishna shrines in Assam. Thousands of devotees throng the temple during the spring festival of Doul Utsav (Holi) to partake in devotional singing (naam-prasanga), smearing of colored powder (phaku), and community prasad. The open ghats offer peaceful riverside contemplation looking across the Brahmaputra.

name: Raimona National Park
shortDescription: Assam's 6th National Park & Sanctuary for the Endangered Golden Langur
fullDescription: Declared as Assam's 6th National Park on World Environment Day 2021, Raimona encompasses 422 sq km of virgin semi-evergreen and moist deciduous forests in the Bodoland Territorial Region (BTR). Contiguous with Bhutan's Phibsoo Wildlife Sanctuary and Jigme Singye Wangchuck National Park, it forms a vital transboundary conservation corridor. Raimona is famous for the charismatic Gee's golden langur, Asian elephants, Royal Bengal tigers, clouded leopards, and over 150 species of rare butterflies.

name: Sikhna Jwhwlao National Park
locality: Ultapani & Chirang Reserve Forests, Indo-Bhutan Border
shortDescription: Assam's 8th National Park & Transboundary Biodiversity Haven (460+ Butterfly Species)
fullDescription: Notified as Assam's 8th National Park in March 2025, Sikhna Jwhwlao spans 316.29 sq km across the pristine foothills of Kokrajhar and Chirang districts in Bodoland. Named after Sikhna Jwhwlao, the legendary Bodo warrior and freedom fighter, the park encompasses the famous Ultapani butterfly valley harboring over 460 butterfly species. Contiguous with Bhutan's Royal Manas National Park, it protects vital transboundary migration corridors for Gee's golden langurs, Asian elephants, Royal Bengal tigers, and greater one-horned rhinos.

name: Tilinga Mandir (The Bell Temple)
shortDescription: Renowned sacred Shiva shrine where millions of brass and copper bells are offered to a sacred banyan tree.
fullDescription: Tilinga Mandir (Bell Temple) in Bordubi, Tinsukia, is one of the most remarkable Shiva pilgrimage sites in Northeast India. Dedicated to Lord Shiva, the temple was founded in 1965 after tea garden workers unearthed a natural stone Shiva Lingam near a sacred banyan tree. Devotees visit from across India, praying for personal aspirations and tying a bell with red or yellow sacred thread around the giant banyan tree branches once their wishes are granted. Over several decades, millions of bells—from tiny tinkling bells to giant ceremonial bronze bells weighing hundreds of kilograms—have covered the temple grounds, creating a resonant sanctuary of profound spiritual faith.

name: Mahabhairav Historic Shiva Temple
shortDescription: Ancient hilltop Shiva temple traditionally attributed to King Banasura, housing one of the largest living Shiva Lingams in the world.
fullDescription: Perched atop a gentle hillock in northern Tezpur, Mahabhairav Temple is one of Assam's oldest and most revered Shaivite shrines. Local tradition and the Kalika Purana date its foundation to the prehistoric ruler King Banasura, a staunch devotee of Lord Shiva. The temple houses an immense stone Shiva Lingam carved from living bedrock, considered one of the largest ancient phallic representations of Shiva in India. Reconstructed in stone during the Salastambha dynasty and restored by Ahom King Tungkhungia rulers, the temple features sculpted stone pillars, serene gardens, and panoramic views over Tezpur city and the Brahmaputra valley.

name: Negheriting Shiva Doul, Dergaon
shortDescription: Magnificent hilltop Pancharatna (five-shrine) Ahom temple surrounded by tea gardens and home to sacred temple monkeys.
fullDescription: Negheriting Shiva Doul is a distinguished Ahom-era architectural marvel situated atop a lush hillock in Dergaon, Golaghat. Originally established during the 8th-9th century Kachari rule and reconstructed into its magnificent current five-domed (Pancharatna) form by Ahom King Rajeswar Singha in 1765 AD under master architect Ghanashyam Khonikar, the complex comprises a central soaring Shiva shrine surrounded by four corner shrines dedicated to Vishnu, Ganesha, Surya, and Durga. Accessible by a grand flight of stone stairs, the temple is surrounded by emerald tea plantations and is famous for its colony of friendly rhesus macaque monkeys protected by temple tradition.

name: Dhekiakhowa Bornamghar, Jorhat
shortDescription: Sacred Vaishnavite prayer hall founded in 1461 AD by Sri Sri Madhabdeva, housing an eternal earthen lamp burning continuously for over 560 years.
fullDescription: Dhekiakhowa Bornamghar in Jorhat is one of Assam's most celebrated sanctums of the Ekasarana Dharma founded by Mahapurush Srimanta Sankardev's chief apostle, Sri Sri Madhabdeva, in 1461 AD. Legend recounts that Madhabdeva sought shelter in this village and was served humble wild fiddlehead ferns (Dhekia Xaak) by a poor elderly devotee couple, after which he sanctified the spot by lighting a sacred earthen lamp (Akhanda Banti) and placing a handwritten copy of the sacred Guru Charita. Remarkably, that very sacred lamp has been continuously maintained, replenished with mustard oil and cotton wicks without interruption for more than 560 years, earning a place in the India Book of Records.

name: Sri Sri Kachakanti Devi Historic Temple
name_hi: श्री श्री कांचाकांति देवी मंदिर, सिलचर
shortDescription: Venerated 19th-century Shakti shrine in Barak Valley harmoniously combining the divine aspects of Maa Durga and Maa Kali.
fullDescription: Located in Udharbond, approximately 11 km from Silchar town in Cachar district, Sri Sri Kachakanti Devi Temple is the foremost pilgrimage sanctuary of the Barak Valley. Dating back originally to 1806 AD during the reign of the Dimasa Kachari kings who consecrated the gold-alloy idol of Goddess Kachakanti—an incarnation harmoniously blending the grace of Maa Durga with the fierce power of Maa Kali—the present brick edifice was restored in 1978. Devotees from all over Assam, Tripura, and Manipur revere the shrine for fulfilled vows, and the temple serves as the spiritual heart of the Barak Valley during Durga Puja, Kali Puja, and local regional festivals.

name: Sri Sri Auniati Satra, Majuli
shortDescription: Premier royal Vaishnavite monastery founded in 1653 AD, famous for the sacred Govinda deity, Apsara dance, and ancient relics.
fullDescription: Established in 1653 AD by Ahom King Jayadhwaj Singha under the guidance of holy saint Niranjan Deva, Sri Sri Auniati Satra is the premier royal Satra of the Brahma-samhati tradition on Majuli river island. Home to hundreds of lifelong celibate monks (Bhakat), the Satra is celebrated for preserving centuries-old Assamese classical performing arts, including the celestial Natua and Apsara dances, Gayan-Bayan devotional percussion, and the grand Raas Leela festival. The Satra houses an extraordinary museum of Ahom royal treasures, inscribed copper plates, gold ornaments, ivory carvings, and antique brass firearms gifted by Ahom monarchs.
